papers.title_en: MedPrune: Topology-Efficient Multimodal Multi-Agent Communication Evolution for Medical VQA Tasks
papers.authors: Jiuheng Wan, Runze Li, Chen Chen, Tingyuan Hu, Daiyang Yu, Yimin Jing, Taolin Zhang, Richang Hong
papers.evidence: 在异构智能体通信图中动态剪枝节点与边
papers.tldr: 医疗多模态大模型推进医学VQA，但现有多智能体框架受冗余通信拓扑拖累，交互模式低效且计算开销偏高。MedPrune把诊断流程建模为异质通信图，以强化学习驱动节点稀疏化剔除与当前问题无关的专科智能体，并通过联合优化任务性能与拓扑复杂度保留关键科室内外连接。全量与少样本医学VQA实验表明，该方法优于多智能体基线，提升token效率并保持较强对抗鲁棒性。
papers.abstract_en: While medical multimodal large language models (Med-MLLMs) advance medical visual question answering (VQA), existing clinical workflow-inspired multi-agent frameworks suffer from interaction patterns and excessive computational overhead caused by redundant communication topologies. In this paper, we propose MedPrune, an efficient medical multimodal multi-agent collaboration framework that dynamically prunes both nodes and edges from the communication topology to enhance reasoning ability and token efficiency. Specifically, we first formulate the diagnostic process as a heterogeneous communication graph, where nodes represent specialist agents from various departments and edges capture intra- and inter-departmental interactions. Building on this graph, we introduce two sparsification mechanisms to enable adaptive collaborative evolution: (1) Heterogeneous Node Sparsification, which eliminates task-irrelevant specialist agents irrelevant to the current multimodal question via reinforcement learning-driven topological optimization, and (2) Heterogeneous Edge Sparsification, which selectively retains only the most diagnostically salient intra- and inter-departmental connections by jointly optimizing task performance and topological complexity. Extensive medical VQA experiments under full-set and few-shot training settings prove MedPrune surpasses multi-agent baselines and boosts token efficiency with strong adversarial robustness.

papers.title_en: Cooperating with Future Collaborators: Multi-Agent RL under Staggered Participation
papers.authors: Jianglin Qiao, Siyi Hu, Thien Hoang Nguyen, Zehong Cao, Salah Sukkarieh
papers.evidence: 交错参与下的合作式多智能体强化学习
papers.tldr: 多智能体强化学习通常假设智能体同时参与，但许多任务中早期智能体先行动并留下对后续智能体有用的信息，形成错峰参与下的跨时间、跨智能体学习依赖。本文提出错峰参与学习 SPL：对早期智能体做前瞻性信息获取监督，对后续接收者做结果监督学习。在多种策略型 MARL 骨干、环境和错峰模式上，SPL 在 60 组 MPE/RWARE 比较中均提升任务完成率，平均高 14.1%，并扩展到八智能体团队和 Isaac Lab 的 UAV-UGV 物理环境。该工作为错峰协作提供了可训练框架。
papers.abstract_en: In cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL), agents are often trained under concurrent participation, while in many tasks some agents act earlier and leave task-relevant information that becomes useful to agents participating later. We study this setting as staggered participation (SP), which introduces a cross-time, cross-agent learning dependency because an early action may affect the return through the information it provides and the later policy that uses it. Learning under SP therefore requires both identifying what information is useful for future decisions and learning how later agents should use it. We propose Staggered Participation Learning (SPL), a training-time augmentation that addresses these two parts with prospective acquisition supervision for earlier agents and outcome-supervised receiver learning for later agents. We evaluate SPL across multiple policy-based MARL backbones, environments, and staggered-participation patterns. Across 60 MPE/RWARE backbone setting comparisons, SPL achieves higher observed mean task completion in every case, with an average difference of 14.1%. The gains also extend to eight-agent teams and a physics-based UAV-UGV environment in Isaac Lab, providing evidence across algorithmic, temporal, and embodied settings.

papers.title_en: Independent Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning with Counterfactual Semantic-Social World Models
papers.authors: Fernando Martinez, Tao Li, Yingdong Lu, Juntao Chen
papers.evidence: 结合反事实语义社会世界模型的全去中心化多智能体强化学习
papers.tldr: 完全去中心化多智能体强化学习仅依赖局部信息，标量奖励难以区分失败源于自身动作、队友配合还是对手反应。CASTLE采用离线训练、在线上下文引导框架，结合局部动力学世界模型与反事实语义-社会世界模型，在冻结后为独立PPO策略提供候选动作后果预测。在Tag、Spread、Adversary三个任务各30个匹配随机种子上，其最终得分均值最高，分别超过最强基线10.67、6.46和0.33归一化分。该工作表明，前瞻性比较候选动作后果可提升独立学习效果。
papers.abstract_en: Fully decentralized multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), also referred to as independent learning, requires each agent to learn and act using only its local information and experience, without a centralized critic or inter-agent communication. Such a stringent information structure renders the conventional reward signal ambiguous. A poor return may result from an ineffective ego action, an incompatible teammate response, or an effective opponent response, yet scalar rewards alone do not reveal which explanation is responsible. We argue that agents can learn more effectively by prospectively comparing the consequences of candidate actions rather than diagnosing failures only from realized returns. We introduce CASTLE (Counterfactual Action-conditioned Semantic Tokens for Local Execution in Decentralized MARL), an offline-training, online-in-context guidance framework with two complementary world models. A Local Dynamics World Model, offline pre-trained over agents' local trajectories, summarizes the agent's local trajectory dynamics and partial observability, while a Semantic-Social World Model predicts compact short-horizon task and social consequences for each candidate ego action. The latter is trained from counterfactual simulator rollouts that expose plausible teammate and opponent responses to alternative actions taken from the same logged rollout state. During online learning and execution, both world models remain frozen and are queried by agents using only locally available information. Their prediction logits provide in-context guidance to an independent PPO policy. Across 30 matched seeds on Tag, Spread, and Adversary in the benchmark multi-particle environments, our proposed CASTLE achieves the highest mean final score among the evaluated methods, exceeding the strongest baseline on each task by 10.67, 6.46, and 0.33 normalized points, respectively.

papers.title_en: DHCG: Dynamic Construction of Hierarchical Collaboration Graphs for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Reasoning
papers.authors: Jie Ren, Jiakang Yuan, Chenyu Huang, Hezeer Ma, Jiayuan Fan, Tao Chen
papers.evidence: 动态构建层次化协作图以编排大模型多智能体系统
papers.tldr: LLM多智能体系统动态编排关键，但现有方法组成受限、依赖错位且规模不灵活。作者将MAS设计重构为部分可观测马尔可夫决策过程，提出DHCG，由Planner、Worker和Generator依据查询与反馈逐步从零构建动态分层协作图。Planner按需生成互补角色并选择性路由信息，可提前终止或扩展，并用动作感知偏好优化训练。在代码生成、数学推理和领域推理基准上平均达SOTA，较单智能体提升13.06分，较静态与动态MAS基线提升2.77-8.02分，并展现跨Planner骨干与未见Worker的泛化能力。
papers.abstract_en: LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) have demonstrated strong capabilities in solving complex problems across diverse domains. Recently, the dynamic orchestration of agent systems has become an important research direction. However, existing methods suffer from limited composition, misaligned dependencies, and inflexible scale, restricting their ability to adapt to reasoning requirements during execution. To address these limitations, we reframe MAS design as a partially observable Markov decision process, in which both the composition and scale of the MAS are dynamically determined. We propose DHCG, a novel framework that coordinates three modules (Planner, Worker, and Generator) to progressively construct a dynamic hierarchical collaboration graph from scratch based on the query and evolving execution feedback. At each step, guided by feedback, the Planner generates a set of distinct and complementary roles tailored to the current reasoning needs and selectively routes relevant information to each role. It can also finalize the hierarchical collaboration graph early or progressively expand it when additional reasoning is required. We further introduce action-aware preference optimization to train the Planner to make more effective decisions when constructing hierarchical collaboration graphs. We systematically evaluate DHCG across code generation, mathematical reasoning, and domain-specific reasoning benchmarks. DHCG achieves state-of-the-art average performance among the compared methods, improving over the single-agent baseline by 13.06 points and outperforming both static and dynamic MAS baselines by 2.77-8.02 points. Additional experiments further demonstrate its generalization across different Planner backbones and unseen Worker models.

papers.title_en: WorkflowOps: Learning Agent Collaboration Priors for Multi-Agent Workflow Orchestration
papers.authors: Qi Cheng, Shengyu Chen, Wei Cheng, Zhengzhang Chen, Xiaowei Jia, Haoyu Wang, Haifeng Chen
papers.evidence: 学习智能体协作先验,借助转移概率引导构建DAG工作流
papers.tldr: 多智能体系统执行复杂任务时，编排层普遍缺乏记忆，每个新任务都要从零开始分解、分配和执行。WorkflowOps 从历史工作流中学习智能体协作先验，用转移概率矩阵指导 DAG 构建，并通过充分性驱动的智能体创建循环和分层语义匹配按需扩充智能体池。在代码、数学和问答混合任务上，其端到端通过率优于近期基线，其中可分解的结构化任务提升最大，且比纯 LLM 路由方案减少 80% 以上 LLM 调用。
papers.abstract_en: Multi-agent systems are increasingly deployed for complex knowledge work, yet their orchestration layers remain largely memoryless: each new task is decomposed, assigned, and executed from scratch with no benefit from prior successful executions. We present WorkflowOps, a multi-agent workflow orchestration framework that learns agent collaboration priors from historical workflows and expands its agent pool on demand to cover new capability requirements. Our approach introduces three coupled mechanisms. First, a transition probability matrix captures pairwise agent collaboration frequencies from past workflows and applies them as soft guidance during DAG workflow construction through intra-layer ordering optimization, probability-thresholded edge suggestion, and transitive reduction for parallelism maximization. Second, a sufficiency-driven agent creation loop detects capability gaps via semantic matching scores, generates specialized agents through an LLM, and simultaneously injects them into the collaboration matrix, so that newly created agents are immediately usable with predicted collaboration priors. Third, a layered semantic matching strategy uses pre-trained sentence embeddings for fast, deterministic capability matching as a first pass, invoking LLM verification only for low-confidence cases, thereby reducing LLM routing calls by over 80\% compared to pure-LLM approaches. Experiments on mixed code, math, and question-answering suites show that WorkflowOps improves end-to-end pass rates over recent workflow-construction baselines, with the largest gains on structured, decomposable tasks where past agent handoff patterns transfer.

papers.title_en: Continual Graph Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Tommaso Marzi, Ahmed Hendawy, Jan Peters, Carlo D'Eramo, Andrea Cini, Cesare Alippi
papers.evidence: 利用任务图结构进行持续多智能体强化学习以迁移协作策略
papers.tldr: 持续多智能体强化学习需在新任务上适应并保留旧任务能力，但现有方法未利用任务结构信息，导致迁移不足与遗忘。作者提出CGMARL框架，将任务序列映射为属性图并据此决定环境动态与智能体数量，同时构建GRAFO基准。进一步提出FROG，用冻结图编码器保留历史结构信息。实验表明FROG与现有持续学习方法结合可显著提升多场景性能，为结构化CMARL提供新范式。
papers.abstract_en: In Continual Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (CMARL), agents learn cooperative policies across sequences of tasks, aiming to adapt effectively to new tasks while preserving the ability to solve previously encountered ones. In many applications, tasks differ in their underlying structure, which can represent, for example, distinct operational conditions or target configurations (e.g., different network topologies in power grids or arrangements in formation control). Existing CMARL methods lack dedicated mechanisms to leverage this structural information when learning new tasks, failing to promote transfer and mitigate forgetting. To fill this gap, we propose Continual Graph Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (CGMARL), a novel framework for CMARL problems in which task sequences are mapped into a series of attributed graphs, each modeling a task-specific structure. In CGMARL, each graph determines the environment dynamics (next states and/or rewards) and the number of agents for the corresponding task. Then, we present Graph-based Formation (GRAFO), the first CGMARL benchmark, and show how forgetting arises in this setting. Finally, to address this limitation, we propose Frozen Graph Encoder (FROG), a method that relies on a frozen graph backbone to preserve past structural information in graph-based CMARL policies. Experiments on GRAFO show that pairing FROG with existing CL methods substantially improves performance on multiple CGMARL scenarios.

papers.title_en: Use and Disuse: Intent-Structured Experience Consolidation for Memory and Learning in LLM Agents
papers.authors: Xiangyi Zeng, Baihang Liu, Xutong Wang, Ze Jin, Yunpeng Li, Qixu Liu
papers.evidence: 面向长期LLM智能体的分层记忆与巩固机制
papers.tldr: LLM 智能体长期自主运行需要把连续经验转化为可复用知识，但完整保留工作细节会带来上下文负担。Hippocam 以嵌套意图组织工作，将已完成意图压缩为任务相关结果与状态，并用递归前缀巩固让久未使用经验逐步抽象。被回忆的经验再整合后会与新经验继续巩固，实现强化、补充和更新。该机制统一工作上下文、长期记忆、知识积累与技能学习，使智能体无需参数更新即可持续学习进化。
papers.abstract_en: The evolution of Large Language Model agents from single-task execution to long-term autonomous operation highlights the critical challenge of transforming continuous experiences into reusable knowledge. To address this, we propose Hippocam, a hierarchical memory and continual learning architecture. Hippocam draws inspiration from two characteristics of human memory: cognitive processes selectively maintain information relevant to current goals, while long-term memories form gradually through repeated consolidation. Accordingly, Hippocam structures an agent's ongoing work as nested intents. The active context remains centered on the current intent, while completed intents are consolidated into the task-relevant outcomes and state needed for subsequent work, rather than carrying forward their full working details. Concurrently, a recursive prefix consolidation mechanism repeatedly consolidates earlier history, causing long-unused experiences to become increasingly abstract. Original interactions are preserved, allowing the agent to progressively recover finer-grained details through the hierarchy and stop once sufficient information is available. Crucially, when past experiences are recalled and reintegrated into active work, they undergo subsequent consolidation alongside new experiences, thereby being reinforced, supplemented, and updated. Through this memory dynamic of use and disuse, Hippocam connects working context, long-term memory, knowledge accumulation, and skill learning within a single continuously evolving experiential process. This enables agents to learn and evolve capabilities through their own experiences without parameter updates.

papers.title_en: Competence-Aware Orchestration for LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
papers.authors: Songmiao Wang, Yuchen Wang, Chenglin Yu, Hongxia Yang, Ming Li
papers.evidence: 依据骨干模型能力自适应调整角色激活与通信图
papers.tldr: LLM多智能体系统常通过角色专业化与协作提升复杂推理，但协作强度应随骨干模型对当前查询的能力动态调整，因为过度协作会带来token成本与冗余交互。本文提出两阶段能力感知编排框架：先估计骨干在当前查询上的任务条件能力，再据此调整角色激活与通信图。六个基准平均得分93.81%；高能力骨干准确率从87.22升至89.97且token成本降36.26%，低能力骨干较现有方法再增4.58分。该工作实现按能力自适应协作，在未见骨干上保持趋势，兼顾效果与成本。
papers.abstract_en: LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) have emerged as a promising paradigm for enhancing complex reasoning through role specialization and collaboration, yet a key challenge remains: how can collaboration be adapted to a backbone's competence on the current query? This problem matters because more collaboration is not always better--richer coordination may help on difficult cases, but it also incurs additional token cost and redundant interactions. We propose a two-stage competence-aware framework for automatic MAS orchestration. It first models the LLM backbone's task-conditioned competence for the current query, and then uses this signal to adapt role activation and the communication graph. Across six benchmarks, our method achieves an average score of 93.81%. Experiments with six LLM backbones of varying competence levels further show that our method adjusts collaboration according to the inferred competence: for higher-competence backbones, it improves average accuracy from 87.22 to 89.97 while reducing token cost by 36.26%; for lower-competence backbones, it yields a further average gain of 4.58 points over existing methods. The same trend also holds on unseen backbones.

papers.title_en: Scaling Multi-Agent Intelligence with Substrate-Centric Coordination
papers.authors: Zhenting Qi, Zhuokai Zhao, Rulin Shao, Kerem Oktar, Zhiyuan Yao, Himabindu Lakkaraju, Wen-tau Yih, Ansong Ni, Bhargavi Paranjape, Yilun Du
papers.evidence: 面向可扩展LLM多智能体系统的基底中心协调机制
papers.tldr: 现有LLM多智能体系统随规模扩大出现阅读负担、信息稀释与失败脆弱性，根源在智能体中心式协调。ScaleMAS将协调迁移到共享数据存储，异步智能体通过发布带引用消息、内容检索和按地址访问交互，并以最多k条结果约束阅读。四类任务中，它以更低推理算力超越基线，扩展至128个智能体并容忍中途失效。该工作为可扩展多智能体协调提供了新范式。
papers.abstract_en: Existing large language model (LLM) based multi-agent systems have been shown to scale poorly, and we identify three problems: reading burden that grows with the group, useful information diluted by shared work of unknown quality, and fragility to failed agents. We argue that the problems are largely due to agent-centric designs: the coordination structure is wired into fixed workflows, central coordinators, or peer-to-peer messaging, and recent blackboard-style methods that move the coordination into a shared medium relieve only the last problem. To close the gaps, we build ScaleMAS, where asynchronous agents interact with a shared datastore of linked messages via three operations: publishing messages with optional references to earlier ones that they build on, searching for messages by content, and visiting messages by address. Search returns at most $k$ messages, so an agent's read stays bounded at any group size; results are ranked by relevance and by how often they are cited, which we find to be an effective proxy for quality; and messages persist after their producers leave, so the group carries on when individual agents fail. Across four agentic tasks, ScaleMAS outperforms agent-centric and blackboard-style baselines at lower inference compute, continues to scale up to 128 agents, and tolerates losing agents midway.

papers.title_en: OpenDGO: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Organizations Across Diverse Application Domains
papers.authors: Xunkai Li, Miao Zhang, Zekai Chen, Xuaner Chen, Yu liu, Rui Qian, Xun Wu, Hongchao Qin, Rong-Hua Li
papers.evidence: 跨领域评测星型链型树型等预设与学习型多智能体组织
papers.tldr: LLM多智能体组织常被预设为Star、Chain、Tree或学习通信图，但缺乏跨领域适用性评估。OpenDGO构建覆盖六类真实领域、三种协作设置的受控基准，在匹配任务、智能体、工具与资源下比较固定与学习组织。结果显示不存在“一刀切”组织，偏好随应用变化，同一通信图在不同角色与输入分配下结果也不同。该工作推动面向应用的按需组织设计。
papers.abstract_en: Large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems are increasingly applied across diverse domains, yet different applications require different forms of agent organization. Existing studies typically adopt predefined organizations, such as Star, Chain, and Tree, or learn communication graphs to improve performance on specific tasks. However, these methods are largely designed and evaluated within a limited set of application domains, providing little understanding of whether an organization effective in one domain remains suitable for others with different collaboration requirements. We present \textbf{OpenDGO}, a controlled benchmark and analysis framework covering six real-world domains and three collaboration settings: Sequential Dependency, Parallel Decomposition, and Information Integration. Under matched tasks, agents, tools, and resource limits, OpenDGO compares fixed and learned organizations while separately examining communication graphs, role assignments, input assignments, resource budgets, and component failures. Our results show that there is no ``one-organization-for-all'' solution: preferred organizations vary across applications, and even the same communication graph can yield different outcomes under different role and input assignments. These findings highlight the need for application-dependent organization design, aiming to understand \emph{which organization is suitable for a given application, under what conditions, and why}.

papers.title_en: Degrees of Freedom in Multi-Agent Coordination: Between Centralized and Decentralized Regimes
papers.authors: Yiqing Peng, Hehai Lin, Zixuan Wang, Dongyi Zhang, Zhengjie Zhu, Yi Han, Yangyang Zheng, Hao Wang, Qian Li, Chengwei Qin
papers.evidence: 研究集中式与去中心化多智能体协调机制之间的连续框架
papers.tldr: 基于LLM的多智能体系统常在集中式与去中心化协调间取舍，集中式易成瓶颈、去中心化协作难控。作者提出自由度DoF连续配置框架，量化下放给下游智能体的决策空间，并统一覆盖两种极端协调机制。跨任务实验显示，中间DoF配置在六种状态中的五种取得高于两端点的平均准确率，且性能景观随任务域变化。该工作为研究和设计中间协调机制提供了可调、可复现的经验依据。
papers.abstract_en: Large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems (MAS) are commonly organized around two coordination regimes. Centralized coordination provides explicit control but can create a bottleneck at a single coordination locus, whereas decentralized coordination offers local autonomy but must achieve effective collaboration through distributed decisions and experience. These trade-offs motivate a systematic study of the space between the two regimes. We introduce Degrees of Freedom (DoF), a continuous configuration framework that quantifies the size of the decision space delegated to downstream agents. DoF controls the granularity of delegated work and the target probability that each task unit is assigned to the branches. Its endpoints recover the two coordination regimes. Across multiple task domains, DoF reveals a hierarchy of organizational effects. Delegated granularity and within-regime routing produce structured but bounded profile reallocations, whereas task domain and retained experience are associated with stronger differences between the centralized- and decentralized-branch profiles. The resulting performance landscape is task-dependent: different domains favor different DoF configurations, while atomic-target conditions are more consistent across runs. In-domain retained experience brings the two branch profiles closer together. The same controlled sweep reveals a task-dependent coordination landscape: some domains exhibit higher-performing configurations, whereas others show flatter responses and no single configuration dominates across domains. In five of the six evaluated state, an intermediate DoF configuration achieves higher mean accuracy than both endpoints, demonstrating the value of exploring the coordination space between them. Together, these findings provide empirical guidance for studying and designing intermediate coordination regimes in LLM-based MAS.

papers.title_en: Optimizing Team Behavior via Extremum-seeking Control in Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Svar Rajankumar Patel, Kshitij Jerath
papers.evidence: 面向合作式多智能体强化学习的自适应行为多样性控制
papers.tldr: 合作多智能体强化学习中，行为多样性有助于角色分工，但其合适水平依赖任务且难以调参。ADiCo采用双时间尺度框架：快速侧DiCo将多样性调节至目标值，慢速侧ESC仅用平均回合回报自适应调整该目标。在两个合作任务的六种配置上，它能在需要同质策略时保持低多样性、需要异质策略时提高多样性，并匹配或超过网格搜索最优DiCo与无约束DiCo。该工作用经典反馈控制替代人工选择多样性目标，为MARL协调训练提供系统化方案。
papers.abstract_en: In cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL), agents must learn to coordinate their actions to achieve shared objectives. A key indicator of effective coordination is behavioral diversity, i.e., the agents' potential to enact distinct yet complementary control policies given the same set of observations. Although behavioral diversity can enable role specialization and richer joint behaviors, its appropriate level is highly context- and task-dependent and often costly to tune. We propose Adaptive Diversity Control (ADiCo), a two-timescale framework that adapts behavioral diversity online during training. On a fast timescale, Diversity Control (DiCo) regulates system diversity toward a target value. On a slower timescale, an Extremum Seeking Controller (ESC) adjusts this target using only mean episodic returns, without requiring an explicit model or analytical gradient of the diversity-performance landscape. We evaluate ADiCo on six configurations across two cooperative MARL tasks, where it maintains task-appropriate diversity levels: low diversity when homogeneous policies are beneficial and higher diversity when heterogeneous policies are required. Through this adaptation, ADiCo matches or exceeds the mean performance of DiCo (best grid-searched diversity target) and Unconstrained DiCo (diversity allowed to emerge without target regulation). These results demonstrate that incorporating classical feedback control into MARL training enables effective coordination by providing a systematic alternative to task-specific manual selection of the diversity target.

papers.title_en: A Responsibility-Centered Coordination Mechanism for Decentralized Multi-Agent Systems
papers.authors: Thi-Nhung Nguyen, Viet-Thanh Pham, Linhao Luo, Thuy-Trang Vu, Dinh Phung
papers.evidence: 面向去中心化多智能体的责任中心协调机制
papers.tldr: 集中式多智能体编排存在扩展与适应性瓶颈，而分散式方法对委派依赖和故障恢复的责任界定不清。RCM以承诺将任务委派与各方显式责任耦合，通过递归委派和本地责任约束决策、RCP通信协议实现去中心化协调。在推理、编码与可执行智能体环境中，RCM任务表现最高提升18.7分、责任指标提升10.2分，并改善故障与危害检测。该工作为无中心控制下可问责的全局协调提供了新机制。
papers.abstract_en: Centralized orchestration provides comprehensive multi-agent coordination but creates bottlenecks in scalability, adaptability, and collective performance. Decentralized approaches alleviate these bottlenecks by distributing coordination across agents, yet often leave responsibility for delegated dependencies and failure recovery unclear. To address this gap, we propose RCM, a responsibility-centered coordination mechanism that leverages commitments to couple task delegation with explicit responsibilities of the involved parties. Through recursive delegation, agents retain their upstream responsibilities while locally orchestrating downstream commitments, thereby preserving accountability across delegation chains, creating a network of local orchestration. We operationalize this mechanism locally through responsibility-constrained decision-making and a responsibility-oriented communication protocol (RCP), enabling agents to autonomously establish, manage, and terminate commitments. As agents act in parallel, their local actions continuously evolve the commitment graph, allowing global coordination to emerge and adapt toward a shared mission without centralized control. Experiments across reasoning, coding, and executable agent environments demonstrate that RCM outperforms strong centralized and decentralized coordination baselines by up to 18.7 points in task performance and 10.2 points in Responsibility, while improving failure and harm detection without task-specific training.

papers.title_en: Learning Self-Orchestration in Decentralized Agent Swarms
papers.authors: Guowei Xu, Zhenting Qi, Amani Kiruga, Himabindu Lakkaraju, Yilun Du
papers.evidence: 在无中心协调者的去中心化智能体集群中联合学习行动策略与自组织
papers.tldr: 现有去中心化多智能体系统常在固定编排结构中训练个体，能力学习与集体组织割裂。为此提出市场式后训练MPT，让智能体通过投标决定谁行动，并用集体结果提供局部训练信用，联合学习动作策略与自编排。在具身制作、机器人导航和深度研究中，MPT优于单体式后训练，且学到的自编排优于替代协调策略。该方法还支持复用、规模扩展与抗掉线鲁棒性。
papers.abstract_en: The capabilities of an agent swarm depend on both its individual members and how they coordinate. Yet existing multi-agent systems often train agents within fixed orchestration structures, separating the learning of individual capabilities from the organization of collective behavior. We introduce market-based post-training (MPT), a framework for jointly learning action policies and self-orchestration in decentralized agent swarms. Agents express their willingness to participate through bids, which determine who acts and how collective outcomes provide local training credit. Learning both action and bidding behavior allows individual capabilities and patterns of participation to adapt together without a central coordinating agent. We evaluate MPT on embodied crafting, robot navigation, and deep research. Results show gains over monolithic post-training and confirm that agent participation indeed evolves with learning. With the same post-trained action policies, learned self-orchestration outperforms alternative coordination strategies. Ablations show that both action and bidding benefit from learning, and that learned bids provide more effective action-training signals. Beyond the original training objectives, trained swarms adapt faster to related tasks and achieve better performance with larger populations at inference time. Larger populations also suffer smaller performance losses under agent dropout, demonstrating that learned self-orchestration supports reuse, scaling, and robustness in decentralized agent swarms. More details are available on our project page at https://guoweixu.com/mpt/.

papers.title_en: Learning Who Talks to Whom: Role-Aware Communication Topology Scheduling for Efficient LLM Multi-Agent Collaboration
papers.authors: Haibin Li, Wenya Yu, Xuefeng Jiang, Jia Li, Xiao Han, Shuai Su, Wei Wei
papers.evidence: 角色感知地调度通信拓扑，决定谁与谁通信以及何时通信
papers.tldr: LLM多智能体依赖通信拓扑交换信息，但静态图难以适应动态求解，且现有方法忽视角色互补、未把图结构纳入团队决策评估，导致推理性能与指数级token开销难以平衡。ACTS在CTDE范式下引入双注意力：角色条件关系注意力按角色与执行状态动态选择可变数量的交互伙伴，拓扑注意力混合器把有向通信图显式嵌入团队价值分解以精确信用分配。在9个基准上平均准确率最高提升6.19个百分点，token消耗降低超15%。
papers.abstract_en: Multi-agent systems driven by large language models (LLMs) rely on structured communication topologies to facilitate information exchange and collaborative reasoning. However, effectively scheduling these topologies to dynamically determine who talks to whom and when to communicate remains a fundamental challenge in balancing collective reasoning performance against exponential token overhead. Existing topology scheduling approaches either enforce static communication graphs that cannot adapt to dynamic problem-solving states, or overlook agent role complementarity while failing to explicitly incorporate the synthesized graph structure into team-level decision evaluation. To tackle these limitations, we propose ACTS, a role-aware adaptive communication topology scheduling framework for efficient LLM multi-agent collaboration. Orchestrated within a Centralized Training with Decentralized Execution (CTDE) paradigm, ACTS introduces a novel dual-attention mechanism. Specifically, a Role-conditioned Relational Attention module dynamically selects variable-cardinality interaction partners based on agent roles and evolving execution states, while a Topological Attention Mixer explicitly embeds the directed communication topology into team value decomposition for precise credit assignment. Comprehensive evaluations across 9 challenging benchmarks covering code generation, multi-step reasoning, general knowledge, and competitive mathematics demonstrate that ACTS consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, boosting average accuracy by up to 6.19 percentage points while reducing token consumption by over 15%. The project website is available at https://acts-mas.github.io/ACTS/.

papers.title_en: BetaMem: Learning to Remember a Changing World for Embodied Agents
papers.authors: Mai Liu, He Sun, Siru Zhong, Kerun Chen, Hao Yan, Xiaohui Lv, Shuai Tao, Wulong Liu
papers.evidence: 具身智能体的长期记忆构建与巩固
papers.tldr: 长时程具身智能体常受时间混淆、记忆记录失真和固定规则重复出错困扰，且存储与检索成本持续增长。BetaMem以工作、空间、实体、情节、经验和程序六层记忆构建可追溯长期记忆，并用双级写入契约、监督微调与强化学习约束记录完整准确。失败驱动策略递归自改进可诊断并局部修复记忆规则。在多个基准上取得领先，且显著提升契约通过率并降低输出开销。
papers.abstract_en: Long-horizon embodied agents face temporal confusion and incomplete or distorted records, recurring errors from fixed memory rules, and growing storage and retrieval costs. We present BetaMem, a framework for building and evolving traceable long-term memory through six linked layers: working, spatial, entity, episodic, experiential, and procedural memory. A dual-level write contract constrains operation executability and source support for content: supervised fine-tuning learns compliant memory operations, while reinforcement learning combines repeated sampling with teacher verification of the original observations to reward complete, accurate records and penalize omissions, distortion, and unsupported content. We formulate failure-driven policy recursive self-improvement through diagnosis along the causal sequence of memory operations and local rule repairs gated by independent replay. Atomic tools frame storage, updates, retrieval, and forgetting as cost-utility allocation under storage and read budgets. Using the open-source Qwen3.5-9B model for memory generation, BetaMem achieves overall scores of 48.08% on M3-Bench-robot, 92.08% on LoCoMo, 72.6% on OpenEQA EM-EQA, and 62.4% on EgoLifeQA, the highest among the listed memory methods under their respective evaluation protocols. Training the model for memory generation raises the contract pass rate from 50.9% to 86.2% while reducing output tokens per stored action by 47.3%. A separate Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct evaluation on EMem-Bench achieves an average success rate of 38.4% and an average error recurrence rate of 24.9%. We perform best among evaluated methods using comparably sized open-source models. Category results show that we have advantages in integrating information across observations, recalling events over long histories, and inferring personal habits.

papers.title_en: Design and Tuning of Multi-Agent Systems Using Bayesian Evolutionary Optimization
papers.authors: Dominik Jehle, Tom Zehle
papers.evidence: 通过工作流图上的贝叶斯进化优化自动发现任务特定的多智能体拓扑
papers.tldr: 多智能体系统设计依赖人工试错且评估昂贵。本文提出贝叶斯进化优化框架，用进化算子生成多样工作流图，并以图感知高斯过程与期望改进聚焦高潜力候选。在BigCodeBench代码生成上取得所评系统最高总体性能，在TabPFN表格预处理多任务上优于默认模型且IID数据保持竞争力。结果表明贝叶斯选择能有效引导昂贵预算下的MAS拓扑搜索。
papers.abstract_en: Designing effective multi-agent systems (MAS) remains a challenging and resource-intensive task. We propose a Bayesian Evolutionary Optimization framework for automatically discovering task-specific MAS topologies. The approach combines evolutionary operators to generate diverse workflow graphs with Bayesian optimization to focus cost intensive evaluations on promising candidates. In contrast to LLM-based candidate selection, our approach uses a graph-aware Gaussian Process and Expected Improvement to provide an explicit selection criterion during evolutionary search. We evaluate the method on BigCodeBench for code generation and on a tabular preprocessing benchmark using TabPFN. On BigCodeBench, evolved architectures achieve the highest overall performance among the evaluated agent systems. On temporal tabular datasets, optimized MAS preprocessing improves over the default TabPFN model on several tasks, while remaining competitive on IID datasets. Overall, the results demonstrate the potential of Bayesian selection for guiding evolutionary MAS search under expensive evaluation budgets.

papers.title_en: RoleFlow: Self-Evolving Multi-Role Agentic Collaboration via Structural Adaptation
papers.authors: Yi Ge, Pan Wang, Xuehao Cui, Zian Zeng, Xu Hu, Heng Huang, Furong Huang
papers.evidence: 通过反馈驱动的结构编辑改进多智能体协作结构
papers.tldr: 现有LLM多智能体系统多依赖预定义协作结构，难适应任务变化，轨迹级奖励也难以定位单次结构修改的贡献。RoleFlow通过反馈驱动的原子编辑与按需角色合成，持续演化多角色协作结构。作者提出SECPO，将每次编辑与同一链状态下的无编辑反事实对照，为编辑相关token分配针对性信用。在四个领域七个基准上平均最优，超越最强基线4.7分，多跳QA领先3.2–7.5 F1，并展现迁移性与泛化性。
papers.abstract_en: Large language model (LLM) based multi-agent systems often rely on predefined collaboration structures, limiting their adaptability to evolving task requirements. Although recent approaches enable dynamic orchestration, trajectory-level rewards they apply assign one outcome to each decision, ofen struggling to identify the contributions of individual structural changes. We propose RoleFlow, a self-evolving multi-role agentic system that refines collaboration structures through feedback-driven atomic edits and on-demand role synthesis. To make structural adaptation learnable, we introduce Single-Edit Counterfactual Policy Optimization (SECPO), which evaluates each edit against its no-edit counterpart at the same chain state and assigns targeted credit to edit-specific tokens. Across seven benchmarks spanning four domains, RoleFlow achieves the optimal average performance, surpassing the strongest competitor by 4.7 points. It leads on all three multi-hop QA benchmarks by 3.2-7.5 F1 points and also shows supremacy on mathematical reasoning, web interaction, and code generation. Further analyses demonstrate cross-benchmark transferability, training-data efficiency, and cross-executor generalization.

papers.title_en: SpecMAGIC: Specification-Guided Multi-Task Generalization in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Zijian Guo, İlker Işık, H. M. Sabbir Ahmad, Wenchao Li
papers.evidence: 面向多样协调需求的多任务泛化分层MARL框架
papers.tldr: 多智能体强化学习中的多任务泛化仍待深入研究，现实任务常含复杂时序扩展与多样协调需求。SpecMAGIC引入结合时序逻辑与协调算子的规范语言，并用分层框架按规范自动机分解子任务：高层集中规划分配兼容子任务序列，低层分散策略执行。在多智能体导航中，其对未见规范显著优于现有方法，智能体增多仍保持性能。该工作为按规范零样本组合复用策略提供新途径。
papers.abstract_en: Multi-task generalization is an important yet underexplored problem in multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL). Many real-world applications require multi-agent systems to generalize across complex, temporally extended tasks with diverse inter-agent coordination requirements. We introduce a specification language that combines temporal-logic task specifications with operators for expressing such requirements. We propose SpecMAGIC, a hierarchical framework that leverages the automaton structure of task specifications for subtask decomposition. A centralized high-level planner identifies and allocates compatible subtask sequences across agents, while decentralized low-level policies execute individual subtasks. This enables zero-shot generalization to new tasks by composing reusable subtask policies according to new specifications, without retraining. We establish soundness and probabilistic completeness of the high-level planner. Experiments on multi-agent navigation tasks show that SpecMAGIC substantially outperforms existing approaches on unseen task specifications and maintains strong performance as the number of agents increases.

papers.title_en: Mining the Design Space of Multi-Agent Workflows
papers.authors: Xavier Cadet, Junyan Cheng, Peter Chin, Kyle Richardson
papers.evidence: 挖掘多智能体工作流拓扑的设计原则
papers.tldr: 多智能体工作流设计长期依赖试错与经验法则，且自动优化器会丢弃搜索轨迹。本文提出两阶段流程，复用AFlow的MCTS在六类算子与26个可验证Enigmata任务上保留中间轮次，构建28,568个可执行工作流语料。再用沙箱AutoResearch在L0惩罚验证目标下挖掘编排代码与提示模板，并在留出搜索中检验原则。结果发现Star-first更差、SharedMemory优于辩论、提示具体性与占位符路由增益显著，表明废弃轨迹可转化为设计原则统计试验台。
papers.abstract_en: Designing large language model (LLM) multi-agent systems (MAS) still relies on trial and error and informal "folk wisdom." Manual studies test only a few communication structures or topologies (e.g., sequential, parallel, shared-memory, or debate), while automated optimizers discard search trajectories after selecting a task-specific workflow. We present a two-phase pipeline for mining reproducible design principles from workflow code and execution traces. We repurpose AFlow's MCTS optimizer across six composable operators and 26 deterministically verified Enigmata tasks, retaining all intermediate rounds to build a corpus of 28,568 executable workflows. A sandboxed AutoResearch loop then mines orchestration code and prompt templates under an $L_0$-penalized validation objective and tests candidate principles on held-out searches. Across 300 feature-mining trials, we identify effects that persist on held-out searches across three levels of workflow design: workflows beginning with independent solvers and one-shot aggregation (Star-first) perform worse ($Δ= -0.045$); persistent shared documents (SharedMemory) outperform debate ($Δ= +0.135$); and prompt specificity and placeholder-based context routing yield gains comparable to communication-structure selection ($Δ= +0.118$). More broadly, our pipeline and results show the feasibility of turning discarded search trajectories into a statistical testbed for discovering and validating multi-agent workflow design principles.

papers.title_en: Understanding Communication Failures in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
papers.authors: Priya Pitre, Jun Hou, Yi Fang, Naren Ramakrishnan, Xuan Wang
papers.evidence: 多智能体LLM系统通信失败分类体系
papers.tldr: 多智能体LLM系统常通过辩论、证据共享与相互纠错提升推理，但交互本身也会引入最终准确率无法解释的失败。作者基于医疗问答、编程、金融、多跳推理、伦理与具身文本等任务中的3211条失败多轮轨迹，构建了通信失败分类体系。分析显示失败主要来自纠错恢复与共识决策问题，而非孤立的首轮错误，且多在智能体首次看到同伴回答后出现。据此提出加强分歧处理、证据核验、少数信号保留与定稿前恢复检查。
papers.abstract_en: Multi-agent LLM systems aim to improve reasoning through debate, evidence sharing, and mutual correction, but interaction can also introduce failures that final accuracy alone cannot explain. Agents may converge too early, ignore dissent, suppress correct minority answers, or preserve a wrong framing across rounds. We present a corpus-grounded taxonomy of communication failures, built from 3,211 failed multi-round trajectories across medical QA, coding, finance, multi-hop reasoning, ethics, and embodied text tasks. Using this taxonomy, we analyze failure distributions across datasets and system designs, round-level error dynamics, recovery hardness, majority transitions, minority-signal suppression, and self-reported confidence. We find that failures are dominated by recovery/correction and consensus/decision problems rather than isolated first-round mistakes, with many emerging after agents first observe peer responses. Based on these findings, we recommend stronger disagreement handling, evidence verification, minority-signal preservation, and recovery checks before finalization.

papers.title_en: EvolveMAS: A Unified Self-Evolution Framework for Decentralized Multi-Agent Systems
papers.authors: Yalun Wu, Qiwei Ma, Bingbing Xu, Dan Zhang, Long Bai, Boyang Wang, Jiatong Li, Zheqi Lv, Shaozu Yuan, Peiying Wang, Jiawei Wang, An Zhang, Tat-Seng Chua
papers.evidence: 面向去中心化多智能体协同与经验复用的统一自进化框架
papers.tldr: 去中心化多智能体系统需要智能体在测试时适应伙伴并复用经验，但现有方法多针对单一交互场景设计适应机制。EvolveMAS为主智能体配备专职MemoryAgent，在推理上下文外维护结构化记忆，并分为幕内在线适应与跨幕知识演化两个过程。在覆盖合作、混合动机与对抗三类设定的五个基准、六种评测配置上，EvolveMAS取得77.2的最高归一化平均分，消融验证了测试时记忆治理与跨幕知识复用的作用。该框架无需更新模型参数，即可统一支持经验驱动的适应与经验复用。
papers.abstract_en: Decentralized multi-agent systems (MAS) enable large language model agents to interact without centralized control. Agents need to adapt to other agents at test time and reuse accumulated experience to refine their interaction strategies for future interactions across cooperative, mixed-motive, and adversarial settings. However, existing approaches often develop adaptation mechanisms for particular interaction settings. This raises a central question: how can decentralized MAS support test-time adaptation and reliable experience reuse across interaction settings? We propose EvolveMAS, a unified self-evolution framework that supports experience-driven adaptation within and across episodes. EvolveMAS pairs each main agent with a dedicated MemoryAgent for test-time memory governance, which maintains isolated Structured Memory outside the main agent's reasoning context. EvolveMAS organizes adaptation into two complementary processes: Within-Episode Online Adaptation and Cross-Episode Knowledge Evolution. During Within-Episode Online Adaptation, MemoryAgent updates episodic, semantic, and working memory from interaction evidence to inform subsequent actions. During Cross-Episode Knowledge Evolution, the main agent uses memory and episode outcomes to distill reusable interaction knowledge comprising partner profiles and interaction strategies for subsequent episodes. Across five benchmarks and six evaluation configurations spanning the three interaction settings, EvolveMAS achieves the highest normalized average score of 77.2 among the compared methods. Ablations show that test-time memory governance and cross-episode knowledge reuse both improve performance. Interaction traces further illustrate how updated memory and distilled knowledge guide subsequent interactions. These results support experience-driven adaptation in decentralized MAS without updating model parameters.

papers.title_en: DynaFlow: Learning Free-Form Multi-Agent Orchestration
papers.authors: Ruhao Liu, Qi Li, Shizun Wang, Xinchao Wang
papers.evidence: 主智能体生成任务级程序编排子智能体,动态调整协作结构
papers.tldr: 多智能体系统常依赖预设协作结构，难以适配多样任务。DynaFlow把自由形式的可执行工作流合成纳入主智能体动作空间，由主智能体自主决定何时协作，并生成顺序或并行执行、结构化信息交换与验证的任务专属程序，执行结果与轨迹再反馈给后续决策。训练上仅用蒸馏轨迹对主智能体做监督微调，再用针对无依据前提、有偏验证和信息流缺陷筛选的样本精炼，所有子智能体保持冻结。六个基准上Forced模式总体准确率88.08%，比最强基线高10.90个百分点。
papers.abstract_en: Multi-agent systems often rely on predefined collaboration structures, limiting their ability to adapt to diverse task requirements. We introduce DynaFlow, a framework that integrates free-form executable workflow synthesis into the action space of the main agent. The agent decides when collaboration is needed and generates task-specific programs that coordinate sub-agents through sequential or parallel execution, structured information exchange, and verification. Execution results and traces inform subsequent actions, enabling the agent to adapt collaboration as reasoning progresses. We train only the main agent through supervised fine-tuning on distilled trajectories, followed by refinement on examples filtered for unsupported premises, biased verification, and information-flow defects. All sub-agents remain fixed, separating orchestration learning from executor capability improvement. Across six benchmarks spanning mathematical reasoning, scientific question answering, and multi-hop retrieval, DynaFlow achieves 88.08% overall accuracy in Forced mode, outperforming the strongest evaluated baseline by 10.90 percentage points with the same Qwen3.5-27B backbone. Workflow analysis finds more explicit use, verification, and refinement of upstream outputs after training, highlighting cross-stage information flow as a key dimension of multi-agent orchestration.

papers.title_en: Multi-Agent Relay Thinking
papers.authors: Xu Liu, Jungang Qiao, Guikun Chen, Xiaojuan Qi, Wenguan Wang
papers.evidence: 接力思维拓扑在智能体间转移推理所有权
papers.tldr: 现有许多多智能体协作采用群体思考拓扑：各智能体独立求解后再聚合输出，难以继承不断演化的推理轨迹。本文提出置信度引导的多智能体中继框架MACR，动态转移推理主导权，并通过中继触发与竞价机制选择下一智能体。在四个基准上，MACR准确率优于最强单模型策略，MathVista提升3.3%、MMStar提升3.9%，且在HallusionBench与MMStar上token开销减少6.0倍。该工作表明中继协作能逐步整合异构智能体的互补能力。
papers.abstract_en: Existing multi-agent collaboration (MAC) methods have primarily explored a group thinking collaboration topology, where agents independently generate solutions and aggregate their outputs. In this work, we investigate an alternative relay thinking topology, where reasoning ownership is dynamically transferred across agents, allowing subsequent agents to inherit and refine an evolving reasoning trajectory. We introduce Multi-Agent Confidence-guided Relay (MACR), a framework that enables dynamical relay collaboration among agents. The key challenge is determining when reasoning should be relayed and which agent should continue the process. method addresses this challenge through confidence-guided relay triggering and a bidding mechanism that selects the next agent based on its confidence. Experiments on four benchmarks show that method outperforms the strongest single-model strategies in accuracy, e.g., +3.3% on MathVista and +3.9% on MMStar, and remains on par with multi-agent strategies while consuming 6.0x less token overhead on HallusionBench and MMStar. Further analysis demonstrates that relay collaboration enables heterogeneous agents to progressively integrate complementary insights, combining heterogeneous capabilities across reasoning stages. Our source code is available at https://github.com/67L1/MACR.

papers.title_en: Belief-Conditioned Multi-Agent Actor Critic for Decentralized LLM Collaboration
papers.authors: Tianle Chen, Shuo Liu, Christopher Amato
papers.evidence: 面向去中心化大模型协作的信念条件多智能体演员评论家方法
papers.tldr: 去中心化LLM协作中，智能体独立执行、通信受限且共享同一目标，现有方法常依赖预设工作流，效率与扩展性不足。BCMAAC将信念建模引入多智能体actor-critic，维护对上下文信息的信念并用于训练。在Minecraft、网页搜索和工具使用任务上，它优于朴素actor-critic基线，多轮且上下文丰富的任务提升更明显。该工作表明信念条件化能改善LLM多智能体协作表现。
papers.abstract_en: Recent work has explored optimizing LLM collaboration through Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL), but many approaches still rely on predefined workflows, limiting efficiency and scalability. Decentralized LLM collaboration is challenging because agents execute independently with limited communication, share a joint objective, and must infer useful information from communication traces. In this paper, we propose BCMAAC, a Belief-Conditioned Multi-Agent Actor-Critic method that maintains beliefs over contextual information and uses them to facilitate training. Experiments on Minecraft game-playing, web searching and tool-using tasks show that BCMAAC improves task performance and collaborative behavior compared to naive actor-critic baselines. The improvements are particularly pronounced in multi-turn tasks with richer contextual information, where belief modeling provides a clear advantage.

papers.title_en: Preference-Guided Cooperation in Multi-Objective Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Qiyue Xia, J. Michael Herrmann
papers.evidence: 面向智能体合作的多目标多智能体强化学习
papers.tldr: 多目标多智能体强化学习通常把协作与目标权衡分开处理，导致复杂度高且难以扩展。本文利用多目标结构本身引导合作，提出目标级反事实信用分配与元梯度方法MIRL（含静态MIRL-S和动态MIRL-D）。智能体学习个体目标优先级，同时协同优化系统级目标。在多目标粒子环境中，该方法提升Pareto前沿质量，动态版本表现最佳。
papers.abstract_en: Multi-objective multi-agent reinforcement learning (MOMARL) addresses agent coordination and objective trade-offs simultaneously while optimising overall system performance. Existing work tends to treat multi-agent cooperation and multi-objective optimisation as largely independent components of a learning problem, which amounts to an exorbitant complexity except in trivial cases. We study here whether the structure provided by multiple objectives can itself be exploited to facilitate cooperation, rather than being treated as an additional optimisation challenge. We formulate MOMARL at both the team and individual levels and introduce objective-wise counterfactual credit assignment to evaluate each agent's contribution across the team objectives. We propose Meta-Gradient Informed Multi-Objective Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MIRL), with static (MIRL-S) and dynamic (MIRL-D) variants. By incorporating meta-gradient information, MIRL enables agents to learn how to prioritise objectives individually while collectively optimising the system-level objective, allowing the multi-objective structure to directly guide cooperation. Experiments on a multi-objective multiple particle environment show that our methods improve Pareto-front quality over baselines, with the dynamic variant achieving the strongest performance.

papers.title_en: Goal-Aware Dynamic Multi-Agent Collaboration for Long-Horizon Tasks
papers.authors: Xu Shen, Lingyong Yan, Shuaiqiang Wang, Jianmin Wu, Zhikai Chen, Jiliang Tang, Jie Ren
papers.evidence: 面向长时程目标完成动态分配职责的多智能体协作
papers.tldr: 针对LLM智能体在长程任务中规划与验证职责难以协调、共享上下文信息易稀释的问题，作者先分析发现验证与成功最相关但常发生较晚，且多智能体仅分离上下文仍会丢失目标或重复调查。为此提出GAD，用增长式执行图组织子任务及依赖，并在各上下文保留原始指令、子任务目标与验收条件。依赖关系决定智能体何时执行及接收哪些结果，验证与恢复模块按目标检查子任务和整体完成情况并触发修复。该工作为长程多智能体协作提供目标感知的动态协调机制。
papers.abstract_en: LLM-based agents are increasingly used to complete complex, long-horizon tasks without human intervention. To make progress toward the task goal, agents need to perform different duties, such as planning and verification, when needed. To understand how single agents manage these duties during long-horizon execution, we conduct a preliminary study. Our analysis shows that verification has the strongest association with task success, but often occurs late, leaving limited opportunities for correction. We also find that the proportion of duty-relevant information decreases as records from different duties accumulate in a shared context. These findings lead us to examine whether multi-agent systems (MAS) can address these problems by assigning duties to agents with separate contexts. Our analysis shows that this separation alone is insufficient. Agents can lose track of the overall goal and repeat prior investigations. They may also lack necessary background while receiving irrelevant information from others. To maintain goal awareness and coordinate collaboration as task needs change, we propose Goal-Aware Dynamic Multi-Agent Collaboration (GAD). It uses a growing execution graph to organize subtasks and their dependencies. To keep agents focused on their goals, each context retains the original instruction and the assigned task's goal and acceptance conditions. To adapt collaboration and information sharing during execution, agents can divide tasks into subtasks and specify dependencies based on execution evidence. These dependencies guide when agents work and which results they receive. Verification and recovery check subtask results and full task completion against their goals, providing feedback for repair when checks fail.

papers.title_en: Federated Agentic AI for Interference-Aware Adaptive Spectrum Coordination
papers.authors: Tomer Baziza Paz, Yaniv Cohen, Kobi Cohen
papers.evidence: 联邦多智能体深度强化学习，智能体感知本地环境并学习协同
papers.tldr: 面向动态异构无线网络，频谱协调需在隐私与通信开销约束下协同学习，但各智能体本地干扰环境不同且决策相互耦合。FASCIA将网络管理器建模为自主智能体，基于本地交互与持久记忆学习频谱策略，并通过周期性联邦聚合共享模型而非原始感知或经验。方法引入近端正则抑制模型漂移，并显式建模部分重叠信道带来的载波间干扰。仿真显示其性能接近集中式基准，且在异构配置下保持有效。
papers.abstract_en: Emerging intelligent wireless networks increasingly rely on autonomous AI agents to adapt spectrum usage to dynamic and heterogeneous operating conditions. However, collective learning is challenging when agents experience different local interference environments and cannot exchange raw observations due to communication-overhead and privacy constraints. We propose Federated Agentic Spectrum Coordination with Interference Awareness (FASCIA), a federated multi-agent deep reinforcement learning framework for adaptive spectrum coordination. In FASCIA, each network manager acts as an autonomous AI agent that perceives its local interference environment, accumulates experience in a persistent local memory, and learns an adaptive spectrum coordination policy through local interactions. Coordination among agents is achieved through periodic federated aggregation of locally trained models, without exchanging raw sensing data or experience. Since spectrum decisions made by one agent alter the environments observed by others, local learning is inherently heterogeneous and coupled. FASCIA employs proximal regularization to mitigate the resulting model drift and explicitly accounts for inter-carrier interference arising from partially overlapping channels. FASCIA is the first federated agentic AI framework to address this challenging interference-coupled spectrum coordination setting. Extensive simulations demonstrate that FASCIA achieves performance close to the centralized benchmark while avoiding raw-experience exchange and maintaining effectiveness across heterogeneous network configurations.

papers.title_en: Long-Term Agent Memory through Complementary Curation and Consolidation
papers.authors: Abhishek Gupta, Dongge Han, Daniel Madrigal Diaz, Wei-Ning Chen, Mayukh Das, Victor Rühle, Saravan Rajmohan
papers.evidence: 面向长期智能体记忆的混合记忆与巩固机制
papers.tldr: 长程对话智能体需要回忆交互历史中的事实、事件与关系，但单一记忆形式难以兼顾覆盖度与效率。本文提出由情节记忆与结构化关系记忆组成的混合记忆架构，并配以巩固机制以保持效率。在 LoCoMo 与 LongMemEval-S 两个基准上，两类记忆始终互补，合并后优于当前最优记忆框架。最终分别取得 90.2% 与 85.5% 的准确率，说明互补式整理与巩固是长期记忆的有效路径。
papers.abstract_en: Long-horizon dialogue agents require effective memory systems to recall facts, events, and relationships from interaction histories. In this work, we propose a hybrid-memory architecture comprising episodic memories and structured relational memories and a consolidation mechanism which preserves efficiency. We conduct an empirical study across two benchmarks: LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S. Our experiments demonstrate that the two memory types are consistently complementary, combining both outperform state-of-the-art memory frameworks and achieves 90.2% accuracy on LoCoMo and 85.5% on LongMemEval-S.

papers.title_en: MASBench: Benchmarking LLM-based Multi-Agent Collaboration under Partial Observability
papers.authors: Qizhi Chu, Zekai Yu, Sijie Wen, Yang Liu, Chen Qian, Cheng Yang, Chuan Shi, Zhiyuan Liu
papers.evidence: 部分可观测下LLM多智能体协作基准
papers.tldr: 现有LLM多智能体基准多假设全局可观测，难以系统评估部分可观测下的协作机制。作者提出MASBench，按推理、调度、博弈三类递进任务组织，并对应评测协议、记忆、路由三种协作机制。基准提供性能分数、通信成本与成本效益等确定性指标，覆盖多种LLM骨干与机制配置。该工作为部分可观测条件下多智能体协作设计与权衡提供可复现的评测依据。
papers.abstract_en: Large language models (LLMs) have progressively evolved into the core of autonomous agents. Building on this progress, LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) coordinate multiple agents into a synergistic team to accomplish complex tasks that exceed the capabilities of individual agents. The effectiveness of such systems depends not only on the agents themselves, but also on how collaboration mechanisms are designed and organized. Note that real-world collaboration is typically partially observable, where each agent can only access partial information about the environment due to physical or privacy-related constraints. However, many existing multi-agent benchmarks assume global observability, and leave limited support for systematically evaluating collaboration mechanisms. To bridge this gap, we introduce MASBench, a multi-agent collaboration benchmark designed under partially observable constraints. It is organized into three progressive task categories: Reasoning, Scheduling, and Game. Through this structure, we progressively evaluate three representative collaboration mechanisms: Protocol, Memory, and Routing. MASBench further provides deterministic evaluation metrics, including performance score, communication cost, and cost effectiveness, to characterize both collaboration outcomes and communication overhead. Experiments across diverse LLM backbones and mechanism configurations offer empirical guidance for effective MAS design. Code is available at: https://github.com/BUPT-GAMMA/MASBench

papers.title_en: Entropy-Gated Belief Coordination for Decentralized Multi-Agent Search Under Intermittent Communication
papers.authors: Mohamed Abdelnaby, Kevin Leahy
papers.evidence: 熵门控信念融合决定去中心化智能体何时通信与协调信念
papers.tldr: 研究间歇通信下去中心化多智能体目标搜索：固定信念融合会在高熵探索期促成过早共识，削弱独立信念覆盖并浪费通信机会。提出熵门控信念协调，在集体熵比高于阈值时跳过融合、仅在开发期合并，并用每步期望互信息 Istep 刻画传感器信息量。EG-TDP 在 103,680 次试验中取得平均信念质量 0.300，较算术平均提升 58.9%、较访问加权融合提升 37.4%，部分配置还优于联合贝叶斯参考。
papers.abstract_en: We study decentralized multi-agent target search where homogeneous agents communicate intermittently at Poisson-distributed times. Standard unconditional belief fusion wastes communication opportunities by synchronizing agents during high-entropy exploration, when diverse independent beliefs provide better coverage than a premature consensus. We introduce \emph{entropy-gated belief coordination}, in which agents skip fusion while their collective entropy ratio exceeds a threshold~\(θ\) and merge only during exploitation, consistent with the bifurcation structure of nonlinear opinion dynamics and the submodular structure of the per-step information gain objective. We further derive \(\Istep(α,β)\), the expected mutual information per observation step between two agents' binary sensors, as an interpretable, communication-free measure of sensor informativeness that motivates the gating design and guides system-level analysis. Experiments across 103{,}680 trials (nine grid sizes up to \(100{\times}100\), Poisson communication timing, four target movement patterns) show that the Entropy-Gated Trust-Decay Planner (\textsc{EG-TDP}), which adds a detection-probability planner switch in exploitation mode, achieves mean belief quality \(\bar{Q}=0.300\) (mean belief mass at the true target cell, averaged across all trials and steps), a \(58.9\%\) gain over arithmetic mean and a \(37.4\%\) gain over visit-weighted fusion. On representative configurations, EG-TDP also outperforms a joint-Bayesian reference that uses all agents'~observations at every step, despite operating under random intermittent contact only.

papers.title_en: Decoupled Multi-Agent Orchestration
papers.authors: Xinle Wu, Yao Lu
papers.evidence: 解耦任务分解与协作决策的学习式多智能体编排
papers.tldr: 现有学习式多智能体编排常把规划绑定固定 worker 池，并用同一终局结果训练任务分解与协作，导致迁移受限、信用分配模糊。DeOrch 将 worker 无关规划与具体 worker 选择解耦：两阶段规划器先在不看 worker 信息时分解任务，再依据紧凑的匹配性反馈选择协作操作。轻量匹配器用固定探针集估计 worker 适配度，并以 contextual bandit 在线更新，新 worker 无需重训。多类分布内/外任务上，它用更少 worker 调用优于先前自动 MAS 编排方法，迁移到全新 worker 池仍有效。
papers.abstract_en: Learned orchestration can automatically construct effective language-model multi-agent systems, but existing approaches couple planning to fixed worker pools and train decomposition and collaboration from the same terminal outcome, limiting transfer and obscuring credit assignment. We introduce DeOrch, which separates worker-agnostic planning from concrete worker selection. Its two-stage planner first decomposes the task without worker information, then chooses collaboration operations using compact, worker-identity-free matchability feedback from the pool, enabling conditional credit assignment to decomposition and collaboration decisions. A lightweight matcher estimates worker suitability from behavior on a fixed probe set and adapts online with a contextual bandit, allowing new workers to be incorporated without retraining the planner or matcher. Across diverse in- and out-of-distribution tasks, DeOrch outperforms prior automatic MAS orchestration methods with fewer worker calls than competing learned orchestrators, remains effective when transferred to an entirely unseen worker pool without retraining, and shows consistent gains from both components.

papers.title_en: OOPMAS: Object-Oriented Multi-Agent Systems for Query-Level Workflow Generation
papers.authors: Qi Cheng, Shengyu Chen, Wei Cheng, Yiqun Xie, Xiaowei Jia, Haoyu Wang, Haifeng Chen
papers.evidence: 按查询生成智能体集合与协作工作流
papers.tldr: 现有LLM多智能体系统多按任务级生成一套固定工作流，统一应用于所有查询，难以应对查询难度差异和混合任务负载。OOPMAS提出免训练框架，按单条查询生成面向对象的智能体集合及其可执行协调工作流，并借助动态技能库从执行反馈中持续积累经验。在覆盖代码、数学与问答的混合任务基准上，它取得89.6%准确率，较最强基线高18.1个百分点，强模型下可达92.4%。
papers.abstract_en: Multi-agent systems (MAS) powered by large language models have shown strong performance across code generation, mathematical reasoning, and question answering. However, existing methods for automating MAS design mostly operate at the task level, producing a single fixed workflow per benchmark that is applied uniformly to all queries. This assumption fails under realistic conditions. Query difficulty varies widely within a task, and real-world workloads mix heterogeneous task types. We introduce OOPMAS, a training-free framework that generates both the agent set and the coordination workflow at the granularity of individual queries. Agents are represented as object-oriented class definitions with dedicated roles, tools, and persistent state, and workflows are expressed as executable main functions over these agent objects. A dynamic skill library accumulates structured lessons from execution feedback across optimization rounds, enabling in-context improvement without any gradient updates or fine-tuning. On a mixed-task benchmark of queries spanning code, math, and QA, OOPMAS achieves 89.6% accuracy, outperforming the strongest baseline by 18.1 percentage points. A model-swap study across four LLM backbones shows consistent scaling, reaching 92.4% with the strongest model.

papers.title_en: Training Advisors for LLM Agents from Task Outcomes
papers.authors: Sergei Polezhaev, Barys Liskavets, Ori Press, Alexander Golubev
papers.evidence: 用强化学习训练LLM智能体的评论者
papers.tldr: LLM智能体需在多步任务中边推理边调用工具，但自然语言反馈常依赖步级标签或参考批评。Caddie把评论家训练成实时顾问，仅以智能体收到建议后的最终成败为奖励，用强化学习优化评论家并冻结基座模型。以Qwen3-4B为评论家、多跳问答训练后，它在四个基座上提升成功率，三个未参与训练；MuSiQue上使Qwen3-4B提升逾25个百分点，超过无评论家的Kimi K3。结果表明按结果训练的评论家可跨模型与领域迁移，并支持推理时自主求助。
papers.abstract_en: Large language model agents tackle multi-step tasks by interleaving reasoning and tool calls with observations from the environment. Prior work has shown that natural-language feedback can help these agents revise their decisions during task execution. We introduce Caddie, a method for training critics to provide natural-language analysis and advice as agents work through a task. Unlike approaches that rely on step-level labels or reference critiques, Caddie learns from whether the agent ultimately succeeds after receiving the critic's feedback. We optimize the critic through reinforcement learning while keeping the base model frozen. Trained on multi-hop question answering with a single base model, our Qwen3-4B critic improves success rates across four base models of different scales and architectures, including three not used during critic training. On the MuSiQue benchmark, the trained critic improves Qwen3-4B's success rate by more than 25 percentage points, surpassing the performance of Kimi K3 without a critic. The same critic also yields gains on out-of-domain interactive benchmarks, including $τ^3$ and DeepDive, with no additional training. Our results show that agents can decide when to seek help from a critic at inference time and that outcome-based critic training can produce guidance that transfers across base models and task domains.

papers.title_en: Tracking State Footprints: How Agents Can Transact
papers.authors: Oto Mraz, Rares Şerban, Kyriakos Psarakis, Burcu Kulahcioglu Ozkan, Asterios Katsifodimos
papers.evidence: 将多智能体协调建模为带状态足迹的数据管理问题
papers.tldr: 多智能体系统已并行执行写代码、改数据库和调用外部服务，但现有编排器不跟踪智能体读写状态，导致丢失更新、陈旧读等并发异常。作者将 MAS 协调视为数据管理问题，提出用 state footprint 刻画智能体在本地上下文、编排器及外部系统中的读写集合。与数据库事务不同，智能体无固定 schema、无隔离快照且失败难确定性重放，但可通过语义消解冲突而非中止。该愿景呼吁下一代编排器与外部系统事务接口支持 agentic transactions。
papers.abstract_en: Can AI agents transact? We argue that they must: as multi-agent systems (MASs) increasingly write code, deploy infrastructure, modify databases, and call web services, lost updates or stale reads can be catastrophic. Although MASs increasingly execute plans in parallel, current orchestrators do not track the state that agents read and write. As a result, concurrency anomalies manifest even in simple coding tasks. We frame MAS coordination as a data management problem and propose to describe agents by their state footprint: the state they read and write across their own local context and state, as well as the state of the orchestrator and external systems. We posit that MASs require guarantees similar to those of databases, but providing them raises new challenges and opportunities: unlike database transactions, agents do not read from a fixed schema or an isolated snapshot, and cannot be replayed deterministically upon failure. They can, however, resolve conflicts semantically instead of aborting, enabling new forms of concurrency control and conflict resolution. Towards agents that can transact, we outline a vision for next-generation agent orchestrators and transactional interfaces for external systems to participate in agentic transactions.

papers.title_en: Token-Efficient Multi-Agent Collaboration via System One-Guided Computational Division of Labor
papers.authors: Zihan Zhou, Xinzhe Hu, Hanxu Yang, Liangjian Wen, Zhao Kang
papers.evidence: 在LLM多智能体协作中将协同操作与推理解耦
papers.tldr: 现有LLM多智能体系统将任务推理与协调操作紧耦合，随交互增长带来显著token开销与延迟。S1-MAS将受限协调决策交给轻量System One控制器与紧凑reader，把开放式推理留给强LLM worker。在七个基准上，相比AgentVerse、DyLAN、SelfOrg，GPT-4o token消耗降低44.9%-97.2%，端到端延迟降低37.8%-93.0%。该工作表明协调可与昂贵推理解耦，为可扩展、低成本的agentic Web应用提供方案。
papers.abstract_en: Large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems (MAS) have become a promising paradigm for complex information-seeking and reasoning tasks by enabling collaborative problem solving among specialized agents. However, existing MAS frameworks tightly couple task reasoning with coordination operations, including task selection, role assignment, message routing, and context management. As interactions grow, using powerful LLMs for these bounded control decisions introduces substantial token overhead and latency, limiting the scalability of agentic Web services. In this paper, we investigate whether coordination can be decoupled from expensive reasoning without compromising collaborative performance. We propose S1-MAS, a token-efficient multi-agent framework based on System One-guided computational division of labor. S1-MAS assigns bounded coordination decisions to lightweight System One models while reserving open-ended reasoning for capable LLM workers. Specifically, a lightweight controller selects inspection conditions, chooses subsequent tasks, and determines termination, while a compact reader retrieves condition-relevant evidence from authorized sources to support these decisions. Through a decision-evidence loop, selected tasks dynamically determine worker roles and source access, enabling adaptive collaboration without task-specific training. Extensive experiments on seven diverse benchmarks demonstrate that S1-MAS achieves superior accuracy while substantially reducing the inference cost. Across individual comparisons with AgentVerse, DyLAN, and SelfOrg on seven benchmarks, S1-MAS reduces GPT-4o token consumption by 44.9%-97.2% and measured end-to-end latency by 37.8%-93.0%. These results highlight its potential for scalable and cost-effective agentic Web applications.

papers.title_en: Topology Design for Distributed Consensus with Relay-Assisted Communication
papers.authors: Shuyi Ren, Zheng Chen, Erik G. Larsson
papers.evidence: 面向分布式共识网络的继电器辅助拓扑优化
papers.tldr: 针对弱连通网络下分布式共识收敛慢的问题，本文研究 relay-assisted 拓扑优化，不再永久添加固定中继链路，而是引入多中继配置按概率激活的分时框架。提出基于 ActiveSet 的算法，增量构建候选中继边集，并联合优化混合矩阵与中继集激活概率，实现自适应中继选择。仿真表明该方法在性能与成本之间取得明显优于固定基数中继选择策略的折中。
papers.abstract_en: This paper focuses on relay-assisted topology optimization to accelerate the convergence of distributed consensus algorithms over weakly connected networks. Instead of permanently adding a fixed set of relay links, we introduce a time-sharing framework where multiple relay configurations are activated in a probabilistic manner. An ActiveSet-based algorithm incrementally constructs candidate relay edge sets and jointly optimizes the mixing matrices and the associated relay set activation probabilities, allowing adaptive relay selection in the optimization process. Simulation results demonstrate a substantially improved performance-cost trade-off compared with fixed-cardinality relay selection strategies.

papers.title_en: Sequential Probabilistic Uncertainty Estimation for Parallel Multi-Agent Reasoning Systems
papers.authors: Tunyu Zhang, Zihao Zhao, Yusong Zhao, Haizhou Shi, Zhuohang Li, Haoxian Chen, Hao Wang, Dimitris N. Metaxas
papers.evidence: 面向并行多智能体推理交互的不确定性估计
papers.tldr: 大模型多智能体系统通过多轮交互提升推理表现，但针对并行多智能体推理的不确定性估计研究仍不足，系统可靠性不仅取决于单次生成，还取决于智能体跨轮次的交互与演化。为此提出免训练、轻量的SAUCE估计器，将系统不确定性建模为对潜在系统级信念的序贯推断，用滤波式更新聚合每轮一致性与生成不确定性信号。在五个骨干模型、五个基准和两种MAS协议上，SAUCE在误分类检测、选择性预测与校准上优于多种基线。该工作为多智能体推理系统提供了有效的不确定性度量。
papers.abstract_en: LLM-based multi-agent systems (MAS) have attracted growing attention for improving reasoning through interaction among multiple agents. In this work, we focus on parallel multi-agent reasoning systems, where several agents solve the same problem over multiple rounds and aggregate their outputs into a final answer. Despite their strong reasoning performance, uncertainty estimation for such systems remains underexplored: the reliability of a MAS depends not only on individual generations, but also on how agents interact and evolve across rounds. We propose SAUCE (Sequential Agent Uncertainty through Consensus Evolution), a lightweight, training-free uncertainty estimator that formulates MAS uncertainty as sequential inference over a latent system-level belief. SAUCE aggregates round-level agreement and generation-uncertainty signals through a filtering-style update. Across five backbones, five benchmarks, and two MAS protocols, SAUCE improves misclassification detection, selective prediction, and calibration over a broad set of uncertainty estimation baselines, including standard log-likelihood-based methods and MAS-specific estimators.

papers.title_en: Understanding Conflict and Compatibility Conditions for Agents in AI-RAN
papers.authors: Arshia Zolghadr, Joao F. Santos, Imtiaz Nasim, Deniz Aytemiz, Nicholas J. Kaminski, Jacek Kibilda
papers.evidence: 分析目标冲突的智能体何时能够共存并共享控制
papers.tldr: AI-RAN开放接口使目标不同的独立代理共同控制RAN参数，现有方法常将控制同一参数者直接判为冲突并仲裁，未评估目标能否同时满足。本文将阈值型代理建模为采样死区反馈控制器，用KPI目标与容差定义可接受死区，推导兼容条件，并证明多代理多KPI兼容性可由成对检验建立。据此提出冲突缓解策略：兼容代理共享参数控制，仅对不可同时满足者仲裁。ns-3仿真显示，兼容且范围可达时SLA漂移近零，不兼容时与Priority Mitigation相当。
papers.abstract_en: Disaggregated mobile networks expose open interfaces for independent agents to control the Radio Access Network (RAN). The interactions between agents with contrasting objectives can result in conflicts. However, existing conflict mitigation methods treat agents that control the same parameter as being in a conflict that requires arbitration of their actions, without assessing whether their objectives can be satisfied simultaneously. In this paper, we introduce a control-theoretic approach to determine when agents can coexist and share control of the same parameters. We model threshold-based agents often encountered in the literature as sampled deadband feedback controllers and represent their objectives through Key Performance Indicator (KPI) targets and tolerances that define acceptable deadband bounds. We derive compatibility conditions from these bounds and show that compatibility for any number of agents and monitored KPIs can be established through pairwise tests. We propose a conflict mitigation policy that allows compatible agents to share control of the same network parameters while restricting arbitration to cases where their objectives cannot be satisfied simultaneously. We evaluate our policy through simulations using NIST's ns3-oran extension of ns-3, and our results show that it enables agents to share control with near-zero Service Level Agreement (SLA) drift when their objectives are compatible and the shared acceptable range is attainable, while matching Priority Mitigation when their objectives are incompatible.

papers.title_en: Stale, Misattributed, or Late: Where Personal Memory Fails Before Generation
papers.authors: Haonan Deng, Park Sinchaisri
papers.evidence: 面向个人智能体记忆的构建与更新解析
papers.tldr: 个人记忆评估常只看最终答案是否正确，掩盖生成前记忆块中的过时、错配与迟到错误。本文以Personal Fact Memory为参考层，直接测量存储有效性与身份解析，并用受控修订基准和LongMemEval/LoCoMo检验。结果显示：不解决更新时70.3%提示暴露旧值；共享活跃存储后participant-aware BM25与参考排序器差距在预设0.02边际内；LLM键分配器键召回高但干净检索率低，开放域合并召回≤0.062。作者据此主张将记忆评估前移到生成前，并分离有效性、身份、弃权与serving延迟。
papers.abstract_en: Personal memory for language agents is usually judged by whether the final an- swer is correct. That score hides errors that arise before generation: the memory block may contain an obsolete value, a fact about the wrong person, or no use- ful fact before the serving deadline. We measure these failures directly. Using Personal Fact Memory (PFM) as a reference layer, we find that temporal validity is primarily a property of memory construction in our setting. On a controlled revision benchmark, serving only the active value of each correctly keyed slot eliminates observed stale exposure; without update resolution, 70.3% of prompts expose a superseded value. Once retrievers share the same active store and par- ticipant information, participant-aware BM25 is equivalent to the reference ranker within a prespecified 0.02 margin. The harder problem is assigning revisions to the right slot. Missed merges leave stale values active, whereas false merges silently remove current values; four LLM key assigners achieve higher key re- call than a rule extractor yet produce lower clean-retrieval rates, and open-domain merge recall on LongMemEval never exceeds 0.062. Misattribution survives va- lidity filtering: an entity posterior reduces same-name exposure on controlled data but cannot distinguish identically named speakers in LoCoMo. Two frozen lan- guage models reproduce prompt errors in generated text. Retrieval latency varies across rankers, but prompt prefill dominates turn-level latency on our hardware. These results argue for evaluating agent memory before generation, separating stored-state validity, identity resolution, abstention, and serving latency.

papers.title_en: Dynamic Mechanism and Information Design in AI-Agent Environments: A General Analytical Framework
papers.authors: Guoqiang Tian
papers.evidence: 面向AI智能体与多智能体互动的动态机制设计框架
papers.tldr: 针对AI代理环境中动态隐藏信息、隐藏行动与信息使用相互交织的机制设计问题，本文构建统一分析框架，将动态筛选、隐藏行动合约与条件动态信息设计纳入共同延续机制。通过动态揭示原理与递归可实施性刻画，并在准线性环境下用动态包络与积分单调性方法得到验证调整的虚拟剩余表示。结果识别动态信息租、验证租与隐藏行动实施成本三类边际，并给出分支层级及监测、信息披露与激励联合设计结论。
papers.abstract_en: This paper develops a general framework for dynamic mechanism and information design with AI agents, encompassing optimal contracting and integrating evolving hidden information and hidden action with partial verification, technological authorization, and multi-agent interaction. It nests conventional dynamic screening, hidden-action contracting, and conditional dynamic information design, while allowing reporting, action, and information-use decisions to interact through a common continuation mechanism. We establish a dynamic revelation principle and a recursive characterization of implementability in which truthful reporting and post-report obedience are jointly determined through continuation incentives. In quasilinear optimal-contracting environments, dynamic envelope and integral-monotonicity methods yield a verification-adjusted dynamic virtual-surplus representation and identify three distinct margins: dynamic information rents, verification rents, and the implementation cost of hidden action. These margins generate a branched hierarchy separating conventional dynamic screening, hidden-action contracting, and their joint problem. We also study the joint design of monitoring, information use, and incentives: more informative monitoring capacity expands the designer's opportunity set, but full disclosure need not be optimal, and information use can itself alter hidden-action incentives. With multiple agents, correlated information, peer discipline, coupled incentives, joint feasibility, and continuation opportunities create additional strategic interactions. Although motivated by AI-agent environments, the framework applies more broadly to dynamic agency settings with similar economic features.

papers.title_en: AgentEvolver: System-Wide Self-Evolution Through Task Execution
papers.authors: Wentao Zhang, Fuchao Yang, Yilei Zhao, Xinrun Wang, Bo An
papers.evidence: 智能体在执行任务中积累可复用能力
papers.tldr: 现有智能体往往能完成任务，却不改进自身的工作方式，任务经验难以沉淀为可复用能力。AgentEvolver 在固定基础模型的前提下，让八类实体通过统一的版本化生命周期接受修订，并由共享 Runtime 协调执行，同时用持久规划和可恢复上下文保留任务方向与证据。它在 SWE-bench Pro Public 上取得 82.08% 的解决率，六个应用案例显示能力可延续到后续网站、游戏与研究任务。其贡献在于把组件层面的能力提升与最终任务成败区分开来。
papers.abstract_en: An agent can complete a task without improving how it works. Turning task experience into reusable capability requires connecting the changed component to its evaluation and subsequent use. We present AgentEvolver, a system for developing capabilities during task execution while keeping the foundation model fixed. Eight entity families expose reusable operations, methods, agents, control flow, interfaces, and supporting state to revision through a common versioned lifecycle. A shared Runtime coordinates ongoing work, while persistent planning and recoverable context preserve task direction and supporting evidence. We evaluate task outcomes on SWE-bench Pro Public and examine capability changes in six application cases. The team reports an 82.08\% resolution rate with evolution, exceeding its reported baseline without evolution. The cases show retained capabilities entering later website, game, and research work, while also documenting incomplete objectives and an unsuccessful strategy. These findings distinguish improvement in a reusable component from success on the final task. AgentEvolver provides a concrete basis for studying capability accumulation through execution; independent-task transfer and total development cost remain open questions.
